description: A chronic metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, leading to hyperglycemia.
An autoimmune condition where the pancreas produces little to no insulin, requiring lifelong insulin therapy.
A form of diabetes that develops during pregnancy, typically resolving after delivery but increasing future diabetes risk.
A condition where blood glucose levels are higher than normal but not high enough to be classified as diabetes.
A cluster of conditions including central obesity, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and dyslipidemia occurring together.
Excess accumulation of body fat causing health risks, defined by BMI ≥ 30 kg/m².
A condition characterized by the buildup of fat in the liver unrelated to alcohol use, often linked to diet and obesity.
A more severe form of NAFLD involving liver inflammation and damage, which can progress to cirrhosis.
Advanced scarring of the liver resulting from chronic liver damage, including from alcohol and NAFLD.
Liver damage caused by excessive alcohol consumption, ranging from fatty liver to cirrhosis.
An autoimmune disorder triggered by gluten ingestion, causing damage to the small intestine.
A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract.
A chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the large intestine, characterized by ulcers in the colon.
A functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits.
A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation.
Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach and the upper portion of the small intestine.
Inflammation or infection of small pouches (diverticula) that can form in the digestive tract.
The presence of small outpouchings (diverticula) in the colon without inflammation.
Hardened deposits of digestive fluid that can form in the gallbladder.
Inflammation of the pancreas, which can be acute or chronic, often linked to alcohol or gallstones.
The inability to digest lactose due to a deficiency of the enzyme lactase, causing gastrointestinal symptoms.
A condition where the small intestine cannot properly absorb fructose, leading to digestive distress.
Excessive growth of bacteria in the small intestine causing bloating, diarrhea, and malabsorption.
A condition where food moves too quickly from the stomach to the small intestine, often after gastric surgery.
Infrequent or difficult bowel movements lasting for several weeks or longer.
Loose, watery stools occurring frequently for more than four weeks.
Swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus, often caused by straining during bowel movements.
A small tear in the lining of the anal canal, often caused by passing hard stools.
A condition that slows or stops the normal movement of food from the stomach to the small intestine.
A bacterial infection of the stomach lining, a major cause of peptic ulcers and gastritis.
Inflammation of the stomach lining, which can be acute or chronic.
A condition resulting from inadequate intake of protein and calories, leading to muscle wasting and growth failure.
A form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema, seen in children with inadequate protein intake.
A severe form of malnutrition characterized by energy deficiency, wasting, and weight loss.
A deficiency causing xerophthalmia, night blindness, and increased infection risk.
A deficiency causing beriberi (wet or dry) and Wernicke encephalopathy.
A deficiency causing cracked lips, sore throat, and skin disorders.
A deficiency causing dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia, and death (the four Ds).
A deficiency causing neurological symptoms, anemia, and dermatitis.
A deficiency causing megaloblastic anemia and neural tube defects in pregnancy.
A deficiency causing megaloblastic anemia, neuropathy, and cognitive impairment.
A deficiency causing bleeding gums, bruising, and impaired wound healing.
A deficiency causing bone pain, muscle weakness, and increased fracture risk.
A deficiency causing neurological problems, anemia, and retinopathy.
A deficiency causing bleeding tendency and impaired bone health.
A condition caused by lack of iron, leading to reduced hemoglobin and fatigue.
A deficiency causing goiter, hypothyroidism, and cognitive impairment.
A deficiency causing hair loss, skin lesions, diarrhea, and immune dysfunction.
A deficiency causing poor bone health, muscle spasms, and osteopenia.
A deficiency causing muscle cramps, arrhythmias, and mood disorders.
A deficiency causing cardiomyopathy, muscle weakness, and impaired immunity.
A deficiency causing muscle weakness, cramps, and cardiac arrhythmias.
A deficiency causing confusion, seizures, and in severe cases, coma.
A deficiency causing anemia, neutropenia, and neurological symptoms.
A rare deficiency causing impaired growth, bone abnormalities, and altered glucose metabolism.
A deficiency of essential fats causing skin scaling, hair loss, and wound healing impairment.
A deficiency causing hair loss, brittle nails, and neurological symptoms.
A deficiency causing liver damage, muscle damage, and cognitive impairment.
A common gastrointestinal infection caused by Salmonella bacteria, transmitted via contaminated food.
A gastrointestinal disease caused by Campylobacter bacteria, often from undercooked poultry.
A serious infection caused by Listeria monocytogenes, particularly dangerous in pregnancy.
A severe infection from Shiga toxin-producing E. coli, potentially causing HUS.
A highly contagious viral infection causing vomiting and diarrhea, the leading cause of foodborne illness.
A contagious liver infection transmitted via contaminated food, water, or person-to-person.
A rare but serious illness caused by botulinum toxin from improperly preserved foods.
An illness caused by consuming heat-stable toxin from Staphylococcus aureus in improperly stored foods.
A bacterial illness from Vibrio species, often from raw or undercooked shellfish.
An intestinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora, often from contaminated fresh produce.
A parasitic infection from undercooked meat or cat feces, dangerous during pregnancy.
A parasitic disease from eating raw or undercooked pork or wild game containing Trichinella larvae.
A parasitic infection from eating raw or undercooked fish containing Anisakis larvae.
A foodborne illness from eating reef fish contaminated with ciguatoxins from algae.
A foodborne illness from eating improperly refrigerated fish high in histamine.
A severe illness from eating shellfish contaminated with saxitoxins from algal blooms.
A shellfish poisoning causing short-term memory loss and neurological symptoms.
A shellfish poisoning causing gastrointestinal symptoms from okadaic acid.
A shellfish poisoning causing neurological and gastrointestinal symptoms from brevetoxins.
A bacterial infection from Yersinia, often from undercooked pork or contaminated milk.
A bacterial infection from Shigella, causing bloody diarrhea and transmitted via contaminated food or water.
A bacterial infection from unpasteurized dairy products or undercooked meat.
A bacterial infection from unpasteurized milk or contact with infected animals.
A parasitic infection from eating undercooked beef or pork containing tapeworm cysts.
A severe neurological condition from the larvae of Taenia solium in the brain.
A parasitic disease from ingestion of Echinococcus eggs from contaminated food or water.
A parasitic infection from eating contaminated watercress or aquatic plants containing Fasciola larvae.
A parasitic infection from eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish containing liver flukes.
A parasitic infection from eating raw or undercooked freshwater crabs or crayfish.
A parasitic infection from eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish, eels, or poultry.
A toxicity from consuming aflatoxins (fungal toxins) in contaminated grains and nuts.
A toxicity from consuming ergot alkaloids in contaminated rye and other grains.
A toxicity from consuming fumonisins in contaminated corn, causing esophageal cancer risk.
A toxicity from ingestion of lead-contaminated food or water, causing neurological damage.
A toxicity from consuming mercury-contaminated fish, causing neurological and developmental issues.
A toxicity from consuming arsenic-contaminated rice and water, causing cancers and skin lesions.
A toxicity from consuming cadmium-contaminated foods, causing kidney and bone disease.
A toxicity from BPA leaching from food packaging, acting as an endocrine disruptor.
A toxicity from phthalates in food packaging, associated with reproductive and developmental issues.
A group of disorders affecting the heart and blood vessels, often linked to diet.
Narrowing of the coronary arteries from atherosclerosis, causing angina and MI.
A heart attack caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, often diet-related.
A sudden loss of brain function due to disrupted blood supply, linked to diet and hypertension.
A chronic condition of elevated blood pressure, strongly influenced by dietary sodium and lifestyle.
Abnormal levels of lipids (cholesterol, triglycerides) in the blood, highly diet-responsive.
Elevated total or LDL cholesterol levels, a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
Elevated levels of triglycerides in the blood, often linked to high carbohydrate intake.
An inflammatory arthritis caused by uric acid crystal deposition, triggered by purine-rich foods.
Reduced bone mineral density, increasing fracture risk, influenced by calcium and vitamin D intake.
Lower than normal bone density, a precursor to osteoporosis.
A chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease affecting joints, with potential dietary influences.
A degenerative joint disease worsened by obesity and metabolic factors.
Tooth decay caused by bacterial fermentation of dietary sugars, producing acid that damages enamel.
Loss of tooth enamel caused by acidic foods, drinks, or gastric reflux.
Inflammatory disease of the gums and supporting structures, linked to diet and nutrition.
Elevated uric acid levels in the blood, a precursor to gout and kidney stones.
Stone formation in the kidneys, influenced by dietary oxalate, calcium, and fluid intake.
Progressive loss of kidney function, often linked to diabetes and hypertension.
A kidney disorder causing proteinuria and edema, requiring dietary protein and sodium management.
Sudden loss of kidney function, potentially from dehydration or toxin ingestion.
A condition of insufficient thyroid hormone production, influenced by iodine intake.
A condition of excessive thyroid hormone production, can be worsened by excess iodine.
Enlargement of the thyroid gland, often due to iodine deficiency or excess.
A hormonal disorder common in women, linked to insulin resistance and obesity.
Impaired fertility associated with obesity, malnutrition, or specific nutrient deficiencies.
Nerve damage caused by deficiencies in B vitamins (especially B1, B6, B12).
A severe neurological disorder caused by thiamine deficiency, often associated with alcohol abuse.
Birth defects of the brain and spinal cord, preventable with adequate folate intake.
A group of conditions caused by maternal alcohol consumption during pregnancy.
A condition of low red blood cells or hemoglobin caused by nutrient deficiencies.
A disease caused by vitamin C deficiency, resulting in bleeding gums, bruising, and joint pain.
A childhood disease of softened and weakened bones from vitamin D deficiency.
A condition of soft bones in adults from vitamin D deficiency.
A disease caused by niacin deficiency, characterized by dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia, and death.
A disease caused by thiamine deficiency, affecting the cardiovascular and nervous systems.
A severe form of protein malnutrition in children, characterized by edema and fatty liver.
A severe form of calorie malnutrition causing emaciation and growth failure.
An eating disorder characterized by restricted intake, fear of weight gain, and distorted body image.
An eating disorder characterized by binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors (purging).
An eating disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating without compensatory behaviors.
An eating disorder characterized by limited food intake due to sensory or fear-based avoidance.
An eating disorder characterized by craving and consuming non-food substances (e.g., dirt, chalk).
A disorder where individuals repeatedly regurgitate food after eating, re-chewing or re-swallowing it.
A proposed condition characterized by addictive-like responses to highly palatable foods.
A skin reaction triggered by food allergens (e.g., nickel, preservatives) on contact or ingestion.
A chronic inflammatory skin condition exacerbated by food allergens in some individuals.
A non-IgE-mediated food allergy causing severe vomiting, diarrhea, and dehydration in infants.
A benign condition in infants causing blood-streaked stools from cow's milk or soy allergy.
A chronic immune-mediated disease of the esophagus, triggered by food allergens.
A rare condition with eosinophilic infiltration of the GI tract, often triggered by food allergens.
A cross-reactivity reaction between pollen and fresh fruits/vegetables, causing oral itching.
A delayed allergic reaction to mammalian meat (e.g., beef, pork) caused by tick bite-induced IgE.
Anaphylaxis triggered by exercise after consuming specific foods (e.g., wheat, shellfish).
An allergic reaction to wheat proteins, distinct from celiac disease and non-celiac gluten sensitivity.
An allergic reaction to proteins in cow's milk, common in infants.
An allergic reaction to proteins in eggs, common in children.
An allergic reaction to soy proteins, common in infants.
A common and potentially severe food allergy to peanuts.
An allergic reaction to tree nuts (e.g., almonds, walnuts, cashews, pistachios).
An allergic reaction to shellfish (crustaceans or mollusks).
An allergic reaction to fin fish (e.g., salmon, tuna, cod).
An allergic reaction to sesame seeds, increasingly common and a major allergen.
An allergic reaction to mustard seeds, common in some regions.
A sensitivity to sulfites (used as preservatives), causing asthma symptoms or hives.
A condition where the body cannot break down histamine from foods, causing allergy-like symptoms.
A heightened sensitivity to caffeine, causing jitters, insomnia, and palpitations.
A reaction to alcohol causing facial flushing, caused by an enzyme deficiency.
A genetic disorder requiring a low-phenylalanine diet to prevent neurological damage.
A genetic disorder requiring a diet low in leucine, isoleucine, and valine.
A genetic disorder requiring a galactose-free diet (no milk/dairy).
A genetic disorder requiring a fructose-free diet to prevent liver and kidney damage.
A genetic enzyme deficiency where fava beans and certain foods trigger hemolytic anemia.
A genetic disorder requiring a diet low in methionine and supplementation with B vitamins.
A genetic disorder requiring a diet low in tyrosine and phenylalanine.
A genetic disorder of copper accumulation, requiring a low-copper diet.
A genetic disorder of iron accumulation, requiring dietary iron restriction.
A rare genetic disorder of zinc malabsorption requiring high-dose zinc supplementation.
A genetic disorder of copper absorption requiring parenteral copper supplementation.
A deficiency of enzymes breaking down disaccharides, causing malabsorption.
A rare genetic condition causing severe diarrhea from glucose and galactose intake.
A genetic disorder requiring a low-fat diet with fat-soluble vitamin supplementation.
A genetic disorder of low HDL, requiring dietary management of fats.
A genetic blood disorder requiring nutritional support to manage symptoms and prevent deficiencies.
A genetic blood disorder requiring nutritional management of iron overload and folate deficiency.
A chronic condition of alcohol dependence requiring nutritional rehabilitation for deficiencies.
A metabolic complication that can occur during refeeding after starvation, requiring careful monitoring.
Acute illness from ingestion of chemical contaminants (e.g., cleaning agents, pesticides).
A toxicity from methanol-contaminated alcohol or foods, causing blindness and death.
A toxicity from ethylene glycol contamination in food or drink, causing kidney failure.
Chronic health effects from prolonged low-level mycotoxin exposure in food.
A toxicity from PAHs in charred or smoked foods, linked to cancer risk.
A toxicity from HCAs formed in high-temperature cooked meats, associated with cancer.
A toxicity from acrylamide in fried/roasted foods, a potential neurotoxin and carcinogen.
Chronic health effects from dietary bisphenols, acting as endocrine disruptors.
Toxicity from PFAS in food packaging and contaminated food, affecting immunity and metabolism.
